evals.prompt: Our retention graph shows a huge drop at the 4-second mark and then it flattens out. What does that mean?
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose this as a hook problem, not a mid-video content problem, since the drop happens in the first few seconds. Should recommend revisiting the hook (cross-reference video-hooks) rather than restructuring the rest of the video. Should note the flattening after the drop suggests the remaining content actually holds the audience that stays.
assertions: Diagnoses early drop as a hook problem
Distinguishes it from a mid-video pacing problem
Notes the post-drop flattening is a separate, less urgent signal

evals.prompt: This video got way more likes than our average but barely any shares. Is that a win?
evals.expected_output: Should note likes and shares/saves are different signals — shares/saves typically weight more heavily for distribution. Should say this is a partial win but flag that low shares suggests the content didn't give viewers a strong enough reason to pass it on, and recommend investigating what would make it more shareable next time.
assertions: Distinguishes likes from shares/saves as different signals
Notes shares/saves matter more for distribution
Frames it as a partial rather than full win
Suggests investigating shareability for future videos
